speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what is causing your discomfort, tell me: have you been passing gas or stool normally, and do you notice any specific shape changes in your bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds painful for you. Have you noticed if you are passing any stools, and if so, are they black and tarry or just small amounts of sticky, foul-smelling stool?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the update; the lack of fever or vomiting helps narrow this down. Given your history of passing foul-smelling, sticky stools and abdominal pain on touch, do you notice if your baby has trouble passing gas or if the stool looks pale and clay-colored?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
